To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have generated a transgenic human embryonic stem cell (hESC) that overexpress Hoxa9 and the enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP), that allows an efficient visualization of human ES cells by fluorescent microscopy, that can be quantified by flow cytometry, and that allows cell differentiation tracking.
we developed a transgenic hESC line that overexpress HoxA9-egfp and a control hESC line overexpressing egfp.
the transgenic cell lines allow an effective visualization, quantification and differentiation tracking of hESCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of novel tools for studying human embryonic development and the use of these tools to understand the role of Hoxa genes in this process.
the generation and characterization of H9-Hoxa9-EGFP transgenic cell line and its use as a tool for studying human development.
the study of the Hoxa9 expression in hESCs and its possible roles in human embryonic development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transgenic hESC lines described in this study are suitable tools for studying human developmental processes and for the identification of genes that play a critical role in human embryogenesis.
HoxA9- and EGFP-transgenic human ES cell lines are useful tools for studying early human development and differentiation.
the use of the H9-Hoxa9-EGFP transgenic hESC line is a valuable tool to study the role of Hoxa genes during human development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HoxA9 overexpression does not alter the differentiation of hESCs.
HoxA9 overexpression in hESCs is compatible with the pluripotency state and that the H9-Hox9-EGFP cells can be used as a useful tool to study human development.
we have developed two novel tools for the study of human development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transgenic cell lines are a useful model for studying human development.
the transgenic hESC lines are a useful tool to study human development in vitro.
the H9-Hoxa9-EGFP transgenic line will allow us to study the role of Hox genes in human development.
